question: What fields are combined in nursing informatics?

options.B: Public health, epidemiology, and health economics
options.C: Nursing science, computer science, and information science

explanation: Nursing informatics merges nursing principles with computer and information technology to improve data management and patient care outcomes. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why do we use computer software in clinical nursing today?

options.A: To replace the need for professional clinical judgment entirely
options.B: To help organize care, reduce errors, and streamline communication
options.C: To increase the time nurses spend filling out paper documents
options.D: To eliminate the requirement for direct patient interaction

explanation: You've got this! Software tools are just there to help make your data handling easier and more accurate, giving you more time for what really matters—caring for your patients. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h1)

question: What is the main use of Microsoft Word in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Creating animated multimedia presentations for patients
options.B: Drafting clinical documents, policies, and reports
options.C: Analyzing large numeric data sets and statistical formulas
options.D: Storing secure long-term electronic health records

explanation: Think of Microsoft Word as your go-to digital notepad for writing reports, guidelines, and letters! It is built specifically for text documents. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h2)

question: How do tables and bullet points help when writing clinical documents?

options.A: They encrypt the document to prevent unauthorized access
options.B: They remove the need for grammar and spelling checks
options.C: They make complex medical information clean and readable
options.D: They automatically convert text into numerical clinical data

explanation: Great formatting is a lifesaver! Breaking down heavy medical text with bullet points helps busy nurses find important details in a flash. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h2)

question: What do we call the basic grid system of rows and columns in Excel?
explanation: Excel is all about spreadsheets! The rows and columns give you a neat grid to organize and crunch numbers easily. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h3)

question: A head nurse wants to quickly find the average temperature of ten patients without doing manual math. Which tool should she use?
explanation: Excel formulas are brilliant for this! They do the heavy lifting and math for you in seconds, saving you time and stress. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using Microsoft PowerPoint in healthcare?

options.A: Tracking daily financial budgets and supply inventories
options.B: Creating visual presentations for education and meetings
options.C: Writing formal legal contracts and employment policies
options.D: Storing confidential patient diagnostic test results

explanation: PowerPoint is your best friend for teaching! It helps you put together engaging slides for class presentations and health talks. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why should you avoid putting too much text on a single PowerPoint slide?

options.A: It prevents the use of basic mathematical formulas
options.B: It violates international health privacy regulations
options.C: It distracts the audience from the speaker's main points
options.D: It automatically corrupts the file format during transfer

explanation: Keep slides clean and simple! Too much text overwhelms your listeners and takes away from what you are actually saying. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which of these is a safe and secure computer habit for clinical staff?

options.A: Sharing personal login passwords with trusted colleagues
options.B: Writing computer access codes on public office sticky notes
options.C: Leaving patient medical records open on unattended screens
options.D: Logging out of the computer workstation when leaving the desk

explanation: Always locking your screen or logging out keeps patient data safe from prying eyes when you step away. Great habit to build early! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h5)

question: When is it ethically okay for a nurse to open a patient's electronic health record?

options.A: Whenever the patient is a personal friend or family member
options.B: Only when actively involved in that patient's direct clinical care
options.C: During routine breaks to pass the time between shifts
options.D: At any time to satisfy personal curiosity about a diagnosis

explanation: Patient privacy is sacred! You should only look at records for patients you are directly caring for as part of your duties. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h5)
